bull.b: Revenue has scaled from about $1.9B in 2021 to $4.9B in 2025 and $5.69B TTM, while Q2 2026 revenue grew 36% year over year. This sustained expansion indicates growing platform reach and gives Roblox a larger base from which engagement, creator activity, and monetization can compound.

Operating cash flow reached $2.10B TTM and free cash flow $1.82B, with both rising materially from prior periods. Positive cash generation despite reported losses provides funding for product and infrastructure investment, supports developer economics, and gives the platform more resilience as it scales.

Roblox combines 123M DAUs with 29B hours and a broadening content mix: the top 10 games' share of hours fell from about 30% to 20% over three years. Broader engagement reduces reliance on individual hits and can strengthen the network connecting users, creators, and experiences.

bear.b: Roblox still reports a TTM operating margin near -20% and net margin near -21%, despite gross margins of roughly 74%–78%. Persistent operating and net losses show that scale has not yet translated into durable profitability, limiting confidence in earnings conversion over the next several quarters.

Under-13 bookings per hour were below forecast after mix shifted toward lower-yield newer and evergreen experiences, while discovery changes reduced impressions for short-term monetizing games. This weakens near-term monetization and shows that engagement growth may not convert proportionally into bookings.

Management expects AI model training, cloud GPU capacity, and fixed-cost deleveraging from lower bookings to compress Q3 margins, with about half of the pressure attributed to AI and infrastructure. These investments may support future products, but make medium-term margin recovery less certain.
